ukmt-pink-2024-02.prompt: The figure shows a square with four circles of equal area, each touching two sides of the square and two other circles. What is the ratio between the area of the black region and the total area of the grey regions?

ukmt-pink-2024-05.prompt: Sadinie is asked to create a rectangular enclosure using 40 m of fencing so that the side-lengths, in metres, of the enclosure are all prime numbers. What is the maximum possible area of the enclosure?

ukmt-pink-2024-07.prompt: The diagram gives the lengths of six lines meeting at a point. Eric wishes to redraw this diagram without lifting his pencil from the paper. He can choose to start his drawing anywhere. What is the shortest distance he can draw to reproduce the figure?

ukmt-pink-2024-09.prompt: The ages of Jo, her daughter and her grandson are all even numbers. The product of their three ages is 2024. How old is Jo?

ukmt-pink-2024-10.prompt: The sum of the digits of the positive integer $N$ is three times the sum of the digits of $N+1$. What is the smallest possible sum of the digits of $N$?

ukmt-pink-2024-12.prompt: A point is chosen inside an equilateral triangle. From this point we draw three segments parallel to the sides, as shown. The lengths of the segments are 2 m, 3 m and 6 m. What is the perimeter of the triangle?

ukmt-pink-2024-14.prompt: The sides, in cm, of two squares are integers. The difference between the areas of the two squares is $19\ \text{cm}^2$. What is the sum of the perimeters of the two squares?

ukmt-pink-2024-18.prompt: For some positive integer $n$, the prime factorisation of the number $n!=1\times2\times\dots\times n$ is of the form shown in the figure; the primes are written in increasing order. Ink has covered some of the primes and some of the exponents. What is the exponent of 17?

ukmt-pink-2024-19.prompt: Kevin makes a net using a combination of squares and equilateral triangles, as shown in the figure. The side length of each square and of each triangle is 1 cm. He folds the net up to form the surface of a polyhedron. What is the distance between the vertices $J$ and $K$ in this polyhedron?

ukmt-pink-2024-20.prompt: Jill has some unit cubes which are all black, grey, or white. She uses 27 of them to build a $3\times3\times3$ cube. She wants the surface to be exactly one-third black, one-third grey, and one-third white. The smallest possible number of black cubes she can use is $X$ and the largest possible number of black cubes she can use is $Y$. What is the value of $Y-X$?

ukmt-pink-2024-22.prompt: Given the integers from 1 to 25, Ajibola wants to remove a few and then split those that remain into two groups so that the products of the integers in each group are equal. Ajibola removes the smallest possible number of integers in order to achieve this. What is the sum of the numbers which Ajibola removes?

ukmt-pink-2024-24.prompt: There are $n$ distinct lines in the plane. One of these lines intersects exactly 5 of the $n$ lines, another of these intersects exactly 9 of the $n$ lines, and yet another intersects exactly 11 of them. Which of the following is the smallest possible value of $n$?

ukmt-pink-2024-25.prompt: Suppose $m$ and $n$ are integers with $0<m<n$. Let $P=(m,n)$, $Q=(n,m)$ and $O=(0,0)$. For how many pairs of $m$ and $n$ will the area of triangle $OPQ$ be equal to 2024?
